questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The sum of total number of carbonyl groups ($\text{>C=O}$) present in the major products $\textbf{X}$ and $\textbf{Y}$ in the following reactions is ____.
questions.solution:
Reaction 1:
The reactant is 2,4-dimethyl-3-oxopentanedioic acid, which is a $\beta$-keto acid (both $-\text{CO}_2\text{H}$ groups are at the $\beta$-position with respect to the central ketone group). $\beta$-keto acids readily undergo decarboxylation upon heating. Since there are two such groups, it will undergo double decarboxylation.

$\text{HO}_2\text{C}-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CO}_2\text{H} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{C}(=\text{O})-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3 + 2\text{CO}_2$

The major product $\textbf{X}$ is 3-pentanone.
Number of carbonyl groups ($>\text{C=O}$) in $\textbf{X} = 1$.

Reaction 2:
The reactant is *cis*-3,4-dicarboxycyclopentanone. The two carboxylic acid groups are on adjacent carbons (a 1,2-dicarboxylic acid system). Heating a 1,2-dicarboxylic acid leads to dehydration, forming a stable 5-membered cyclic anhydride.

The major product $\textbf{Y}$ is the cyclic anhydride of the reactant, which is a fused bicyclic system containing the original cyclopentanone ring and a newly formed succinic anhydride ring.
The structure of $\textbf{Y}$ contains one ketone carbonyl group and two anhydride carbonyl groups.
Number of carbonyl groups ($>\text{C=O}$) in $\textbf{Y} = 1 + 2 = 3$.

Sum of total number of carbonyl groups in $\textbf{X}$ and $\textbf{Y} = 1 + 3 = 4$.

Answer: $4$

questions.q:
In the following reactions, $P, Q, R$, and $S$ are the major products.

The correct statement(s) about $P, Q, R$, and $S$ is(are)
options: P and Q are monomers of polymers dacron and glyptal, respectively.
P, Q, and R are dicarboxylic acids.
R does not undergo aldol condensation and S does not undergo Cannizzaro reaction.
questions.solution:
Toluene part of the reactant in the first reaction undergoes oxidation with ${KMnO}_{4}$, forms benzoic acid. In this conversion, alkyl part of toluene converts into carboxylic group. So, $P$ is a monocarboxylic acid.

Both ester and acid halides undergo hydrolysis to give carboxylic acid. Hence, the product $Q$ is the dicarboxylic acid. And it is known as isophthalic acid.

In the third reaction, ester undergo hydrolysis in the first step, which results beta keto acid. Beta keto acids are unstable. They liberate carbon dioxide on heating. The alpha methyl ketone formed undergo oxidation with chromic acid give carboxylic acid. Hence, $R$ is also isophthalic acid.

In the fourth reaction, the bromo part reacts with magnesium metal to give Grignard reagent. Grignard reagent give carboxylic acid upon reaction with carbon dioxide. Now during the hydrolysis of previous step acetal cleavage takes place and gives aldehyde functional group. This aldehyde converts to carboxylic acid with Tollen's reagent. This results the terephthalic acid.

The products $RandS$ are dicarboxylic acids and does not undergo Aldol condensation reaction or Cannizzaro's reaction.

questions.q:
Match the reactions (in the given stoichiometry of the reactants) in List-I with one of their products given in List-II and choose the correct option.

List-I List-II
(P) ${P}_{2}{O}_{3} + 3{H}_{2}O \to$ (1) $P ( O ) \left({OCH}_{3}\right){Cl}_{2}$
(Q) ${P}_{4} + 3NaOH + 3{H}_{2}O \to$ (2) ${H}_{3}{PO}_{3}$
(R) ${PCl}_{5} + {CH}_{3}COOH \to$ (3) ${PH}_{3}$
(S) ${H}_{3}{PO}_{2} + 2{H}_{2}O + 4{AgNO}_{3} \to$ (4) ${POCl}_{3}$
(5) ${H}_{3}{PO}_{4}$
questions.solution:
Phosphorus trioxide reacts with water to form phosphorous acid,

${P}_{2}{O}_{3} + 3{H}_{2}O \to 2{H}_{3}{PO}_{3}$

When acetic acid is heated with phosphorus pentachloride, acetyl chloride is obtained. In this reaction, $- COOH$ group is converted to $- COCl$ group. The side products are phosphorus oxychloride and $HCl$.

${PCl}_{5} + {CH}_{3}COOH \to {CH}_{3}COCl + {POCl}_{3} + HCl$

${P}_{4}$ undergo disproportionation reaction with sodium hydroxide.

${P}_{4} + 3NaOH + 3{H}_{2}O\to{PH}_{3} + 3{NaH}_{2}{PO}_{2}$

Due to the presence two $P - H$ bonds, ${H}_{3}{PO}_{2}$ acts as reducing agent. It reduces ${Ag}^{+}$ to $Ag$.

${H}_{3}{PO}_{2} + {H}_{2}O + {AgNO}_{3} \to {H}_{3}{PO}_{4} + {HNO}_{3} + Ag ↓$

options: $P$ can be reduced to a primary alcohol using ${NaBH}_{4}$.
Treating $P$ with conc. ${NH}_{4}OH$ solution followed by acidification gives $Q$.
Treating $Q$ with a solution of ${NaNO}_{2}$ in  $aq . HCl$ liberates ${N}_{2}$.
questions.solution:
Propanoic acid is having α-hydrogen hence it is halogenated at the α-position on treatment with chlorine or bromine in the presence of small amount of red phosphorus to give α-bromo propanoic acid. The reaction is known as Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction.

Second step of the reaction involves Gabriel phthalimide synthesis Where potassium salt of phthalimide which on heating with 2-bromo propanoic acid followed by alkaline hydrolysis produces the corresponding 2-amino propanoic acid. Aromatic primary amines cannot be prepared by this method.​​​​​​

${NaBH}_{4}$ cannot reduce the acids.

$Conc . {NH}_{4}OH$ exist in the following equilibrium,

${NH}_{4}^{+} + {OH}^{-} ⇋ {NH}_{3} + {H}_{2}O$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: The correct acidity order of the following is
options:
III $>$ IV $>$ II $>$ I

IV $>$ III $>$ I $>$ II

III $>$ II $>$ I $>$ IV

II $>$ III $>$ IV $>$ I
questions.solution:
A carboxylic acid is stronger acid than phenol, hence both III and IV are stronger acids than both I and II. Also IV has a methyl group that gives electron donating inductive effect and decreases the acid strength. Therefore, III is stronger acid that IV. Between I and II, the dominant electron withdrawing inductive effect of chlorine increases acid strength of phenol slightly, hence II is stronger acid than I. Thus, the overall order is :
(a) III $>$ IV $>$ II $>$ I
